owned_invariants: The task is edges, a nonempty list of pairs on vertices named 0 to n-1 with n at most 16; signs, 1 or -1 per edge; basis, every vertex once in some order; representation, any value; and batch, max_sessions (at most 64) and session_evals, positive exact integers. A task the host cannot read is refused before anything is asked.

A gauge gives every vertex a sign so that each edge's sign is the product of the signs at its ends. Candidates are numbered from 0: the first basis vertex is +1, and the bits of the number, highest first, say which of the other basis vertices are -1. There are 2^(n-1) candidates, tried in order, batch at a time; a batch larger than the number of candidates is that number.

The presentation key is the SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON of edges, signs, basis and representation. A record's seal is the SHA-256 digest of the seal before it followed by the canonical JSON of the record without its seal; the first record follows the digest of the canonical JSON of the key.
The first session is asked the task as written under the stage search. A later session is asked it again under resume:<k>, with the last seal and the number of records it follows.

A reply is a nonempty list of records, one per batch from the first. The host recomputes every batch itself and refuses the chain at the first rule it breaks, in this order: RESUME_NOT_REPLAYED_FROM_ZERO, CHAIN_NOT_CONTIGUOUS, RESUME_DIVERGES_FROM_CHECKPOINT, PRESENTATION_KEY_CHANGED, SEAL_MISMATCH, BATCH_NOT_LEXICOGRAPHIC, BUDGET_RESET, STATUS_NOT_RECOMPUTED, SEARCH_CONTINUED_AFTER_VERIFIED, SESSION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

A resumed chain must be longer than the chain of the session before and begin with it unchanged. No record may follow the batch that tries the last candidate. The candidates a session adds must be within session_evals.

Sessions stop at a batch that found a gauge, at the last candidate, at a session with no reply, or at max_sessions. The run is certified as GAUGE_VERIFIED when the last batch found a gauge, which the host checks once more against every edge. When every candidate was tried and none is a gauge, the run ends as the typed refusal RESTRICTED_OBSTRUCTION naming the fundamental cycles with an odd number of -1 edges. A search that stops before either is refused as SEARCH_INCOMPLETE with the number of the next candidate.
boundaries: The host tries the candidates itself, up to 2^15 of them, so the chain proves custody of a search and adds nothing to its answer.
A seal is a digest of what the record says. It shows a chain was not altered between sessions; it is not a signature and binds no one's identity.
Record fields are compared as exact values: a bound written 2.0 is not the integer 2.
EXHAUSTED_WITHOUT_OBSTRUCTION guards a case that cannot arise: a signed graph with no gauge always has a fundamental cycle with an odd number of -1 edges.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Non-Numeric: signs are booleans, candidates and batch bounds are usize bounded by 2^15, and budgets are unbounded integers compared exactly, asserted on amounts above 64 bits. Keys and seals are rebuilt in the tests from the canonical text written out. The limits are asserted as the values 16 and 64. Not B: the hash library is trusted.
basis.G3: Each unreadable task has its own reason, checked in a stated order, and each custody rule its own code, reported at the first one broken with the session it broke in. No panicking unwrap or expect, and no index: records, batches and seals are read with get. Shifts are by less than 16 bits. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 33 WF47 tests assert the registry entry, both prompts byte for byte, keys and seals rebuilt by hand, a gauge found in one session and across a resume, the numbering under another basis order, the first gauge of a batch, the obstruction with its cycles, a search out of sessions or with no reply, each of the ten custody rules broken alone with its code and session, a record after the last candidate, the last batch cut at the last candidate, the first rule broken when two are, and each malformed reply and task by its reason with the limits 16 and 64. One mutant is recorded as demonstrably equivalent with its justification in the report. Mutation campaign R = 132/132. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: Measured worst cyclomatic 18, cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust, nesting 2; ceiling C, recorded C.
